findings.F1: The tested book's deepest fall (−35.3 %, over 201 days from w1 into w3, while the coins fell −62.5 %) comes from the heavy-volume days on which the coin closed up. On those signal bars the next-day excess return is −0.05 % (t −0.56, n 3409), and in w1–w3 they summed a gain of −0.93 against +0.08 for the down-day signal bars. A book trading only up-day signals has Sharpe 0.03, Calmar −0.02 and its deepest fall at −42.4 %.

ideas.idea: The heavier a coin's volume on a day relative to its own prior 20-day average, the more the coin rises over the next day, when that day was a down day, and the more so the larger the day's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds long for the day after a heavy-volume down day, larger the bigger the surge and the fall, and stays out after heavy-volume up days, which carried the book's deepest falls.
ideas.name: volume surge after falling day

ideas.idea: The heavier a coin's volume on a day relative to its own prior 20-day average, the more the coin rises over the next day, the lower the day's close sits within its high-low range.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys heavy-volume days that closed near their low, where the selling was absorbed, larger the bigger the surge, and stays out of heavy-volume days that closed near their high.
ideas.name: absorbed selling, low close
